title: TIGaussian: Disentangle Gaussians for Spatial-Awared Text-Image-3D Alignment
claim: Our method beats prior baselines across many benchmarks and retrieves better matches for ambiguous queries, as higher similarity scores show.
layout: 2 panels: bar chart left, query-to-top-5 retrieval grids right; green stars
description: A dashed vertical line splits the figure in two. The left panel is a grouped bar chart with three bars per task (blue Uni3D, orange UniGS, green Ours). It covers six benchmarks: O-LVIS classification, Objaverse text retrieval, O-LVIS image retrieval, ABO classification, ABO text retrieval and ABO image retrieval. Numeric labels sit above the bars, and the green bars are tallest everywhere. The largest gap is ABO image retrieval, where the green bar reaches 66.2. The right panel has four rows. Each row starts with a speech-bubble query (text or an image) on the left. Next to it are two columns of top-5 retrieved 3D renders. The UniGS column has an orange dashed border and the Ours column has a green dashed border. Rendered beds, a purple car and horses carry similarity scores below them. A green star marks the ground-truth best candidate. In the Ours column the star lands at rank 1.
caption: TIGAUSSIAN enables 3D modal pretraining on several tasks, e.g., zero-shot classification, text-3D retrieval and image-3D retrieval. Left: Compared to prior 3D multi-modal alignment methods – Uni3D and UniGS, TIGAUSSIAN presents superior performance on multiple datasets – Objaverse(-LVIS) and ABO. Right: In challenging scenarios involving ambiguous or complex queries, TIGAUSSIAN demonstrates superior performance owing to its disentangled encoder architecture and specialized cross-modal alignment mechanism. We report the similarity score of each item in the figure.
abstract: While visual-language models have profoundly linked features between texts and images, the incorporation of 3D modality data, such as point clouds and 3D Gaussians, further enables pretraining for 3D-related tasks, e.g., cross-modal retrieval, zero-shot classification, and scene recognition. As challenges remain in extracting 3D modal features and bridging the gap between different modalities, we propose TIGaussian, a framework that harnesses 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) characteristics to strengthen cross-modality alignment through multi-branch 3DGS tokenizer and modality-specific 3D feature alignment strategies. Specifically, our multi-branch 3DGS tokenizer decouples the intrinsic properties of 3DGS structures into compact latent representations, enabling more generalizable feature extraction. To further bridge the modality gap, we develop a bidirectional cross-modal alignment strategies: a multi-view feature fusion mechanism that leverages diffusion priors to resolve perspective ambiguity in image-3D alignment, while a text-3D projection module adaptively maps 3D features to text embedding space for better text-3D alignment. Extensive experiments on various datasets demonstrate the state-of-the-art performance of TIGaussian in multiple tasks.
